Classification: Initialization function

3. Dispatch inventory handlers to clear 10 inventory slots (g_dwInventorySlot1-10)

    - Password text box from g_PasswordTextBoxFactory (string ID 0x148E)
    - Max players text box from g_MaxPlayersTextBoxFactory (string ID 0x148F)

    - Scrollbar from g_GameListScrollbarFactory

    - Iterate through null-terminated string list adding unique entries

16. Initialize screenshot config and scroll to index 0
17. Check if edit box has content by converting Unicode to Win string
    - If string length > 0, set bit mask to 1 (enable join button)
18. Return 1 (success)

Parameters: None (void)

functions.name: McpClientJoinGamePollCallback
functions.comment:

Polls MCP client connection state and exits the message loop when the

2. Call Ordinal_10031 (D2MCPCLIENT) - Check join operation status

   b. If connected AND g_fMcpCancelOperation == 0: Return 1 (continue polling)
4. Call Ordinal_10030(0) (D2MCPCLIENT) - Disconnect/cleanup
5. Call StopMessageLoop (D2WIN) - Exit message pump
6. Return 1

Parameters: None (stdcall callback via MessagePumpLoop)

Returns:

  Ordinal_10003 - Poll/update client state
  Ordinal_10031 - Get join operation status (0 = in progress)
  Ordinal_10002 - Check connection status (non-zero = connected)

   a. Get current edit box text via D2Win_GetEditBoxChild
   b. If no text or no chat history buffer, return 0
   c. Convert edit box Unicode text to ANSI (acStack_600)
   d. Get history text from buffer (acStack_500)
   e. Calculate combined length of current text + history text
   f. If combined length exceeds 255 chars, return 0 (overflow protection)
   g. Split current text at cursor position into prefix and suffix
   h. Build new string: prefix + history + suffix using sprintf
   i. Convert result to Unicode and update edit box
5. Return 0

  nCursorPosition (size_t) - Current cursor position in edit box text
  lpszKeyCode (char *) - Pointer to key code byte triggering callback

Returns:

  1 - Key was not handled (pass to default handler)

Special Cases:

  - History insertion protects against buffer overflow (255 char limit)
  - Empty edit box or missing history buffer causes early return
  - Cursor position used to split text for inline history insertion

Real implementation would validate buffer pointer, check window handle validity,
and configure buffer for window-specific video rendering operations. Current stub
allows applications to call this function without errors while providing no functionality.

functions.name: UpdateUIElementsOnTextChange
functions.comment:
Updates Battle.net UI element visibility based on edit box text content and chat history state.

Classification: Worker function - Called by EnterBattleNetMultiplayerUI and OnEditBoxTextChangedCallback

Algorithm:
1. Get edit box child text from g_pCurrentInputPointer via D2Win_GetEditBoxChild
2. Check if text pointer is non-NULL and string length > 0; set fHasText flag (ESI)
3. Call SetUnitBitMask on g_apBnetUIObjects[5] with fHasText (Join Game button)
4. Call SetUnitBitMask on g_apBnetUIObjects[0] with fHasText (Create Game button)
5. Compute fCanSendChat = (g_pChatHistoryBuffer != NULL) AND fHasText
6. Call SetUnitBitMask on g_apBnetUIObjects[1] with fCanSendChat (Send button)
7. If g_pChatHistoryBuffer exists and has player pointer at offset 0x9C:
   a. Get unit ID from player pointer via GetUnitIdFromPointer
   b. Mask result with gdwBitMasks[9] (bit 9 = 0x200, whisper target flag)
8. Compute fCanWhisper = (g_pChatHistoryBuffer != NULL) AND (dwMaskedId == 0)
9. Call SetUnitBitMask on g_apBnetUIObjects[3] with fCanWhisper (Whisper button)
10. If g_pChatHistoryBuffer exists AND dwMaskedId != 0:
    Call SetUnitBitMask on g_apBnetUIObjects[4] with 1 (Squelch button enabled)
11. Else: Call SetUnitBitMask on g_apBnetUIObjects[4] with 0 (Squelch disabled)

Parameters: None (uses globals)

Returns: void

Globals Accessed:
  g_pCurrentInputPointer (0x6fa218d0) - Current edit box control pointer
  g_apBnetUIObjects (0x6fa216a8) - Array of UI element pointers:
    [0] = Create Game button
    [1] = Send button
    [3] = Whisper button
    [4] = Squelch button
    [5] = Join Game button
  g_pChatHistoryBuffer (0x6fa21aa4) - Chat history structure pointer
    +0x9C = Pointer to selected player unit
  gdwBitMasks_exref (0x6fa1922c) - External bitmask array pointer
    [9] (+0x24) = Whisper target validation mask (0x200)

Special Cases:
  - If edit box is empty, Join/Create/Send buttons are disabled
  - Whisper button enabled only when chat buffer exists but no whisper target selected
  - Squelch button enabled only when valid whisper target is selected

functions.name: ValidateBinkInstallLocation
functions.comment:

- English locale (9) requires different Y positions for lobby elements

functions.name: BinkBufferGetError
functions.comment:
Retrieves pointer to the global Bink buffer error message string.

Algorithm:
1. Return address of global error buffer array g_szErrorBuffer

Parameters:
None

Returns:
char * - Pointer to null-terminated error message string in g_szErrorBuffer
         The buffer contains the most recent error message from Bink buffer operations
         Returns valid pointer to 256-byte character array (never NULL)

Special Cases:
- Function always returns same buffer address (0x1002f01c)
- Error buffer is shared across all Bink buffer operations

functions.name: AddGameToList
functions.comment:
Adds a game entry to the global game list if not already present.

Algorithm:
1. Check if game already exists by scanning game ID list
2. If game ID matches existing entry, return early (duplicate check)
3. Calculate offset for new entry (count * 0x3b stride)
4. Copy game ID (short at input+0x08) to entry+0x33
5. Initialize entry+0x37 DWORD to 0
6. Copy flags (short at input+0x14) to entry+0x31
7. Copy game name string (from input+0x1c) via strlen + memcpy to entry+0x01
8. Copy description string (from input+0x2c) via strlen + memcpy to entry+0x11
9. Increment global game list count

Parameters:
  pGameInfo (ECX) - Pointer to game info structure:
    +0x08: wGameId (short) - Game type/ID for duplicate detection
    +0x14: wFlags (short) - Game flags
    +0x1c: szGameName (char[16]) - Null-terminated game name
    +0x2c: szDescription (char[16]) - Null-terminated description

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Early return if game ID already exists in list
  - String copy uses optimized DWORD copy then byte copy for remainder

Structure Layout (GameListEntry, stride 0x3b = 59 bytes):
  Offset  Size  Field              Type    Description
  0x00    1     padding            byte    Unused padding
  0x01    16    szGameName         char[]  Game name string
  0x11    16    szDescription      char[]  Description string
  0x31    2     wFlags             short   Game flags from input+0x14
  0x33    2     wGameId            short   Game ID from input+0x08
  0x37    4     dwReserved         dword   Initialized to 0

Global Data:
  g_nGameListCount (0x6fa3e9d8) - Current count of games in list
  g_aGameListEntries (0x6fa30140) - Base of game list array

functions.name: InitializeGameListPanel
functions.comment:
Initializes the game list panel UI controls and session handling.

Classification: Initialization function

Algorithm:
1. Check if game list data pointer is valid (GetGameListDataPointer)
2. If invalid (-1), display error message via ValidateStringId(0x1413) and return
3. Create panel base object from g_PanelBaseDescriptor
4. Create game name label from g_LobbyDescriptor0, set text (string ID 0x141f)
5. Create password label from g_LobbyDescriptor1, set text (string ID 0x149a)
6. Create max players label from g_LobbyDescriptor2, set text (string ID 0x1469)
7. Create difficulty label from g_LobbyDescriptor3, set text (string ID 0x149b)
8. Create game list container from g_GameListContainerDescriptor
9. Create and configure current input control (g_ChildObjectType7)
10. Create game name edit box (g_GameNameEditDescriptor) with:
    - Control value 0x10
    - Field value callback at 0x6fa0ef50
    - Data field callback at 0x6fa0f000
11. Create password edit box (g_PasswordEditDescriptor) with:
    - Control value 0x10
    - Field callback at 0x6fa10540
12. Link game name and password edit boxes in double-linked list
13. Create text control from g_TextControlDescriptor
14. If Ordinal_10002 (battle.net session check) returns non-zero:
    - Call Ordinal_10056 to set up session data
    - Call Ordinal_10059(0x87) for session configuration
15. Create secondary control from g_SecondaryControlDescriptor
16. Check if 5000ms elapsed since last refresh (GetTickCount vs g_dwLastRefreshTick)
17. If refresh needed:
    a. Update g_dwLastRefreshTick
    b. Set g_dwInventoryPanelMode = 3
    c. Reset g_nGameListCount = 0
    d. If character is in lobby (offset 0x356 == 2):
       - Clear session buffer (24 bytes)
       - Check expansion flag (offset 0x1ea & 4), set 0x800 if set
       - Increment g_wSessionRequestId (skip 0)
       - Call Ordinal_10006 to request game list
       - Store request ID in g_wLastSessionRequestId
    e. Else call FetchAndFilterGameListByDifficulty
18. Set current input pointer to game name edit box
19. Reset g_nFilteredGameCount and g_nGameListCount to 0
20. Get edit box text content via D2Win_GetEditBoxChild
21. If text exists, convert Unicode to ANSI (max 255 chars)
22. Count text length to determine if filter should be applied
23. Call SetUnitBitMask to enable/disable filtering based on text presence

Parameters: None

Returns: void

Special Cases:
- Early return if GetGameListDataPointer returns -1 (no valid game data)
- Session request ID skips 0 value (wrapped increment)
- Refresh only triggers if 5000ms+ elapsed since last refresh

Magic Numbers:
- 0x1413: Error string ID for invalid game list
- 0x141f: Game name label string ID
- 0x149a: Password label string ID
- 0x1469: Max players label string ID
- 0x149b: Difficulty label string ID
- 0x10: Edit control type value
- 0x87: Session configuration flag
- 4999: Refresh threshold (5000ms - 1)
- 0x356: Offset to lobby state flag in game data
- 0x1ea: Offset to expansion flags in game data
- 0x800: Expansion mode bit flag

Ordinal Calls:
- Ordinal_10002: Battle.net session validation check
- Ordinal_10056: Session data initialization
- Ordinal_10059: Session configuration (parameter 0x87)
- Ordinal_10006: Request game list from server

Globals Modified:
- g_pPanelBaseObject: Panel base control object
- g_pGameNameLabel: Game name text label
- g_pPasswordLabel: Password text label
- g_pMaxPlayersLabel: Max players text label
- g_pDifficultyLabel: Difficulty text label
- g_pGameListContainer: Game list container control
- g_pCurrentInputControl: Current input focus control
- g_pGameNameEditBox: Game name edit field
- g_pPasswordEditBox: Password edit field
- g_pTextControl: Text display control
- g_pGameListSecondaryControl: Secondary game list control
- g_dwLastRefreshTick: Last refresh timestamp
- g_dwInventoryPanelMode: Panel mode state
- g_nGameListCount: Number of games in list
- g_nFilteredGameCount: Number of filtered games
- g_wSessionRequestId: Current session request ID
- g_wLastSessionRequestId: Last session request ID sent

Note: Function body is truncated in Ghidra (single instruction in listing).
Decompiler produces full output but variable renaming limited.

functions.name: InitiateGameListRequest
functions.comment:
InitiateGameListRequest - Initiates a game list request for multiplayer game browsing

Classification: Worker function - prepares request parameters and dispatches to D2MCPCLIENT

Algorithm:
1. Set inventory panel mode to 3 (game list view)
2. Reset game list count to 0
3. Check difficulty mode byte at g_pGameListData+0x356
4. If difficulty != 0x02 (Nightmare): delegate to FetchAndFilterGameListByDifficulty and return
5. For Hell difficulty (0x02): zero 24-byte request buffer (6 DWORDs via REP STOSD)
6. Check expansion flag bit 0x04 at g_pGameListData+0x1EA
7. If expansion flag set: OR dwRequestFlags with 0x800 (expansion filter flag)
8. Increment g_wSessionRequestId until non-zero (handles wraparound)
9. Call D2MCPCLIENT.Ordinal_10006 to send game list request
10. Save current session ID to g_wLastSessionRequestId for response matching

Parameters: None (void function)

Returns: void

Special Cases:
- Non-Hell difficulty: Delegates to FetchAndFilterGameListByDifficulty
- Session ID wraparound: Loop ensures ID is never 0 after increment

Global State Modified:
- g_dwInventoryPanelMode: Set to 3 (game list panel)
- g_nGameListCount: Reset to 0
- g_wSessionRequestId: Incremented (non-zero guaranteed)
- g_wLastSessionRequestId: Updated to match sent request

Flag Bits at offset 0x1EA:
- 0x04: Expansion mode flag (triggers 0x800 in request flags)

Request Flags:
- 0x800: Expansion-only games filter

Ordinal Calls:
- Ordinal_10006 (D2MCPCLIENT.DLL): Sends game list request to server

Called By: Single caller at 0x6fa03812
Calls: FetchAndFilterGameListByDifficulty, D2MCPCLIENT.Ordinal_10006

functions.name: FinalizeFilteredGameListDisplay
functions.comment:
Refreshes the game list UI control with filtered game entries and restores selection.

Worker function called after filtering game list. Copies game entries from source
array to display array, populates UI control with game names and player counts,
then attempts to restore previously selected game by name matching.

Algorithm:
1. Early exit if g_pTextControl is NULL
2. Save currently selected game name (Unicode to ANSI conversion) if any
3. Get current selection index from text control
4. Clear both primary and secondary text data lists
5. Copy g_nGameListCount to g_nFilteredGameCount
6. If no games, exit
7. Check if player count display is enabled (Ordinal_10002)
8. Copy game entries: memcpy source to dest (stride 0x3B = 59 bytes per entry)
   - DWORD copy loop (uVar6 >> 2 iterations)
   - Byte copy loop for remainder (uVar6 & 3 bytes)
9. For each game entry (0 to g_nFilteredGameCount):
   a. Add game name to text control (offset -0x30 from player count = name field)
   b. If player count display enabled, convert count to string and append
10. If previously selected game exists:
    - Search for matching name using strcmp-style comparison
    - Entry names start at g_aGameListEntriesDest + 1 (offset into entry)
    - On match, call SetTextFieldValue to select that index
11. Otherwise set selection index to 0
12. Scroll to selected index

Parameters:
  None (uses global state)

Returns:
  void

Globals Accessed:
  g_pTextControl (0x6fa3e8c0) - Main text list control
  g_pGameListSecondaryControl (0x6fa3e8c4) - Secondary list control
  g_nGameListCount (0x6fa3e9d8) - Source game count
  g_nFilteredGameCount (0x6fa3e9d4) - Filtered count (written)
  g_aGameListEntriesSource (0x6fa30140) - Source game entry array
  g_aGameListEntriesDest (0x6fa21ac8) - Destination entry array

Structure Layout (Game Entry, 59 bytes / 0x3B):
  Offset  Size  Field        Description
  0x00    1     unknown      Entry type or flags
  0x01    47    szGameName   Game name (ANSI string)
  0x30    1     unknown      Padding or delimiter
  0x31    2     wPlayerCount Player count (ushort at offset 0x31)
  ...     ...   ...          Remaining fields

Special Cases:
  - If no games in list, clears UI and exits early
  - If no previous selection, defaults to index 0
  - String comparison is case-sensitive, byte-by-byte

Called By:
  FetchAndFilterGameListByDifficulty (0x6fa0e838)
  FUN_6fa03249, FUN_6fa0327a

functions.name: ValidateGameNameCharacter
functions.signature: bool ValidateGameNameCharacter(int nUnused1, int nUnused2, char * lpszChar)
functions.comment:
Validates a character for game name input fields.

WARNING: Function boundaries are incomplete in Ghidra analysis. Only the first
instruction (MOV ECX, [g_pTextControl]) is included in the function body.
The actual function extends from 0x6fa0ef50 to 0x6fa0efb4 (100 bytes).

Algorithm (from manual disassembly):
1. Load g_pTextControl global into ECX
2. Set EDX = -1 (sentinel value)
3. Call helper function (0x6fa129c6)
4. Get character from lpszChar parameter [ESP+0x0C]
5. Subtract 0x20 (space character) to normalize range
6. If (char - 0x20) > 0x3F, go to secondary validation
7. Use jump table lookup at 0x6fa0efb4 for character class
8. Secondary validation checks:
   - If char is '0'-'9' (0x30-0x39): return TRUE
   - If char is 'a'-'z' (0x61-0x7a): return TRUE
   - Otherwise: return FALSE

Parameters:
  nUnused1 (int) - Unused parameter (stack cleanup)
  nUnused2 (int) - Unused parameter (stack cleanup)
  lpszChar (char *) - Pointer to character to validate

Returns:
  bool - TRUE (1) if character is valid for game name, FALSE (0) otherwise

Valid Characters:
  - ASCII printable range 0x20-0x5F via lookup table
  - Digits '0'-'9'
  - Lowercase letters 'a'-'z'

Lookup Table at 0x6fa0efbc (64 bytes):
  Maps characters 0x20-0x5F to valid (01) or invalid (00)
  Pattern: 00 01 01 01 01 01 01 00 01 01 01 01 01 00 ...
  Space (0x20) = invalid, most punctuation = valid

Jump Table at 0x6fa0efb4:
  0x6fa0efa6 - Handle lowercase letter range
  0x6fa0ef7e - Handle primary table lookup

Called By:
  FinalizeFilteredGameListDisplay via MOV EDX, 0x6fa0ef50 at 0x6fa0eb86
  Used as callback for edit box character validation

Calling Convention: __stdcall (RET 0xC = 12 bytes, 3 DWORD params)

functions.name: ValidateEditBoxTextAndSetMask
functions.comment:
Validates edit box text content and sets UI element bit mask based on text presence.
Called as callback when edit box content changes. Checks if game name field has text.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve Unicode text from g_pGameNameEditBox via D2Win_GetEditBoxChild
2. If text pointer is NULL, set mask type to 0 (no text)
3. Convert Unicode to ANSI using unicode2Win with 255 char max
4. Calculate string length using REPNE SCASB pattern:
   - Initialize counter to -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)
   - Scan for null terminator, decrement counter each byte
   - NOT and DEC to get actual length
5. If string length >= 1, set mask type to 1 (has valid text)
6. Call SetUnitBitMask on g_pGameListContainer with mask type
7. Always return 1 (TRUE) indicating callback handled

Parameters: None (uses global UI state)

Returns: Always 1 (TRUE) - callback success indicator

Special Cases:
- NULL text pointer: Sets mask to 0 without string processing
- Empty string (length 0): Sets mask to 0
- Any text >= 1 char: Sets mask to 1

Globals Referenced:
- g_pGameNameEditBox (0x6fa3e8d4): Edit box control for game name input
- g_pGameListContainer (0x6fa3e8cc): UI container receiving the bit mask update

functions.name: CompletePendingSessionRequest
functions.comment:
CompletePendingSessionRequest - Finalizes a pending MCP session request and stores the request ID

Classification: Worker function - called to complete pending session requests for response matching

Algorithm:
1. Check if pending session request ID is valid (not -1)
2. If invalid, return immediately (no pending request)
3. Call D2MCPCLIENT.Ordinal_10007 to finalize the pending request
4. Store the pending request ID in upper word of g_wLastSessionRequestId (offset +2)
5. Clear the pending request ID by setting to -1 (marks as completed)
6. Return

Parameters: None (void function)

Returns: void

Global State Modified:
- g_nPendingSessionRequestId: Cleared to -1 after processing
- g_wLastSessionRequestId: Upper word (offset +2) set to completed request ID

Special Cases:
- No-op when g_nPendingSessionRequestId is -1 (no pending request)
- Upper word storage allows tracking both current and last request IDs

Ordinal Calls:
- Ordinal_10007 (D2MCPCLIENT.DLL): Finalizes/completes pending session request

Related Functions:
- InitiateGameListRequest: Sets g_wLastSessionRequestId._0_2_ (lower word)
- This function sets g_wLastSessionRequestId._2_2_ (upper word)

Called By: Single caller at 0x6fa03836

functions.name: OnGameListSelectionClick
functions.comment:
OnGameListSelectionClick - Handles user click events on the game list selection control.

Classification: Event Handler/Callback

Algorithm:
1. Get currently selected game index from text control
2. Clear secondary game list display
3. If no valid selection (0xFFFFFFFF), return early
4. Check if this is a double-click:
   a. Message type must be WM_LBUTTONDOWN (0x201)
   b. Same item as last click (compare indices)
   c. Within 501ms (0x1F5) of last click
5. If double-click detected, call FUN_6fa10b50 (join game handler) and return
6. Save current tick count and selected index for next click comparison
7. Check network status via Ordinal_10002 (D2Multi network check)
8. If network available (non-zero):
   a. Get selected item's Unicode name from text control
   b. Convert Unicode to ANSI in local buffer
   c. Increment session request ID (avoiding zero)
   d. Copy game name to global buffer
   e. Set pending session request ID
   f. Update game name edit box
9. If network unavailable (local mode):
   a. Get game description from g_aszGameListDescriptions array
   b. Calculate string length (inline strlen)
   c. If description not empty, display in secondary control
   d. Get game name from g_aGameListEntriesSource array
   e. Set game name in edit box

Parameters:
  pMsgInfo (int) - Pointer to message info structure
    +0x04: Message type (0x201 = WM_LBUTTONDOWN)

Returns:
  int - Always returns 0

Special Cases:
  - Double-click threshold: 501ms (0x1F5)
  - Invalid selection: 0xFFFFFFFF
  - Game entry stride: 0x3B (59 bytes)
  - Game name offset within entry: +1 byte

Globals Modified:
  g_dwLastSelectedGameIndex - Tracks last clicked index
  g_dwLastClickTickCount - Tracks last click time
  g_szSelectedGameName - Stores selected game name (256 bytes)
  g_wSessionRequestId - Incremented request ID
  g_nPendingSessionRequestId - Pending request tracking

functions.name: PopulateGameListDetails
functions.comment:
Populates the game list secondary control with detailed game information.

Displays game name, elapsed time, level restrictions, max players, and
character roster with class names for a selected multiplayer game entry.

Algorithm:
1. Check if g_pGameListSecondaryControl exists, return if null
2. Clear existing text data from the control
3. Check game name at offset +0x2C for non-empty string
4. If game name exists, add game name and newline to control
5. Calculate elapsed time from seconds at offset +0x0C:
   - Hours = seconds / 3600
   - Minutes = (seconds % 3600) / 60
   - Seconds = seconds % 60
6. Format and display "Elapsed Time: H:MM:SS"
7. Check level restriction byte at offset +0x11 (max level diff)
   - If 0: Display single level from offset +0x10
   - If 1-99: Display level range "Level X to Y"
   - If >= 100: Skip level display
8. Check max players byte at offset +0x12
   - If 1-7: Display "Up to N Players"
9. Add newline separator
10. Loop through player roster (count at offset +0x14):
    - Character names at offset +0x8C (16-byte stride)
    - Character class at offset +0x4C (2-byte stride)
    - Character level at offset +0x6C (2-byte stride)
    - Format class-specific string based on class ID (0-6)
    - Display using StringAsciiToUnicode with style 5
11. Reset scrollbar to top position

Parameters:
  pGameInfo (ECX) - Pointer to GameListEntry structure containing:
    +0x0C: dwElapsedSeconds - Elapsed time in seconds
    +0x10: byMinLevel - Minimum character level
    +0x11: byMaxLevelDiff - Maximum level difference (0=single, 1-99=range)
    +0x12: byMaxPlayers - Maximum players (1-7)
    +0x14: dwPlayerCount - Player count in game
    +0x2C: szGameName[32] - Game name string
    +0x4C: awCharClass[8] - Character class IDs (0-6)
    +0x6C: awCharLevel[8] - Character levels
    +0x8C: aszCharName[8][16] - Character names (16 bytes each)

Returns: void

Special Cases:
  - Empty game name (length 0): Skips game name display
  - Level diff >= 100: Skips level restriction display
  - Max players 0 or >= 8: Skips player count display
  - Empty character name: Skips that player entry

Character Class IDs:
  0 = Amazon, 1 = Sorceress, 2 = Necromancer, 3 = Paladin
  4 = Barbarian, 5 = Druid, 6 = Assassin

functions.name: ClearBnetUIControlsAndSetDefaultInput
functions.comment:
Clears all Battle.net multiplayer UI controls and sets default input focus.

Classification: Internal Utility - UI state reset helper

Algorithm:
1. Dispatch inventory item handler for g_pPanelBaseObject to clear base panel
2. Dispatch inventory item handler for g_pGameNameEditBox to clear game name input
3. Dispatch inventory item handler for g_pPasswordEditBox to clear password input
4. Dispatch inventory item handler for g_pTextControl to clear text display
5. Dispatch inventory item handler for g_pGameListSecondaryControl to clear secondary list
6. Dispatch inventory item handler for g_pGameListContainer to clear main game list
7. Dispatch inventory item handler for g_pCurrentInputControl to clear current input
8. Dispatch inventory item handler for g_pGameNameLabel to clear game name label
9. Dispatch inventory item handler for g_pPasswordLabel to clear password label
10. Dispatch inventory item handler for g_pMaxPlayersLabel to clear max players label
11. Dispatch inventory item handler for g_pDifficultyLabel to clear difficulty label
12. Set current input item to g_apBnetUIObjects[10] (default input focus)

Parameters: None

Returns: void

Callers: Called by 14+ panel initialization and reset functions including:
- EnterBattleNetMultiplayerUI, InitializePanelMode2
- ResetInventoryPanelState, ResetInventoryPanelAndShowSelection
- InitializeGameJoinSession, InitializeGameJoinAndCopySessionData
- SetInventoryPanelVisibility, InitializePanelDisplayDefault

Purpose: Ensures consistent UI state by clearing all Battle.net multiplayer

External Calls:
- DispatchInventoryItemHandler (D2WIN.DLL) - Clears/resets UI control state
- SetCurrentInputItem (D2WIN.DLL) - Sets keyboard input focus to control

functions.name: UpdateMaxPlayersToggleState
functions.comment:
Updates UI controls based on max players toggle button state.

When the max players toggle is enabled (checked):
- Disables difficulty buttons (sets bit mask to 0)
- Enables max players edit boxes (sets bit mask to 1)
- Sets text boxes with string 0x148b using color 4 (enabled style)

When the max players toggle is disabled (unchecked):
- Enables difficulty buttons (sets bit mask to 1)
- Disables max players edit boxes (sets bit mask to 0)
- Sets text boxes with string 0x148b using color 5 (disabled style)

Algorithm:
1. Check if g_pMaxPlayersToggleButton is valid via IsButtonValid
2. If toggle is VALID (enabled):
   a. Clear bit mask on g_pDifficultyButton1 and g_pDifficultyButton2
   b. Set bit mask on g_pMaxPlayersEditBox1 and g_pMaxPlayersEditBox2
   c. Set unit bit mask on g_pMaxPlayersInputField, EditBox1, EditBox2
   d. Get localized string 0x148b, add to TextBox1 with color=4
3. If toggle is INVALID (disabled):

functions.comment:

1. Call setup function FUN_6ff2b372() to initialize cleanup state
2. Check global termination flag g_dwTerminationActiveFlag - if set to 1, terminate immediately with TerminateProcess
3. Set global cleanup flag g_dwCleanupFlag = 1 to signal cleanup is active

   - Process dynamic function pointer buffer from g_pbDynamicBufferEnd to g_pbDynamicBufferStart
   - Call each non-null function pointer in reverse order (typical destructor pattern)
   - Call static cleanup function pointer arrays from g_ppStaticCleanupArrayStart to g_ppStaticCleanupArrayEnd
6. Always call final cleanup function pointer arrays from g_ppFinalCleanupArrayStart to g_ppFinalCleanupArrayEnd
7. If nTerminateFlag == 0: set g_dwTerminationActiveFlag = 1 and call ExitProcess (no return)
8. Otherwise: call FUN_6ff2b37b() final cleanup and return to caller

dwExitCode (uint): Exit code passed to ExitProcess/TerminateProcess (0-255)
nQuickExit (int): Cleanup mode flag - 0 = full cleanup with dynamic destructors, non-zero = skip dynamic cleanup
nTerminateFlag (int): Termination mode - 0 = ExitProcess (no return), non-zero = return to caller

- If g_pbDynamicBufferStart is null: skips dynamic buffer processing safely

- Uses ExitProcess for normal process termination after cleanup

- Buffer boundary checks prevent memory access violations during traversal

functions.name: RunConstructorArray
functions.comment:
Executes an array of constructor or initialization function pointers in sequence.

Algorithm:
1. Iterate through function pointer array from ppfnStart to ppfnEnd (exclusive)
2. For each 4-byte aligned function pointer entry:
   a. Load the function pointer value into EAX
   b. Test if pointer is non-null (TEST EAX,EAX) 
   c. Skip null pointers (JZ to increment)
   d. Call the function pointer (CALL EAX) with no parameters
3. Advance to next function pointer (ADD ESI,0x4)
4. Continue until reaching end pointer (CMP ESI,[ESP+0xc])
5. Return when all valid function pointers have been executed

Parameters:
- ppfnStart (void * *): Pointer to start of function pointer array
- ppfnEnd (void * *): Pointer to end of function pointer array (exclusive)

Returns:
- void: No return value

Special Cases:
- Null function pointers are safely skipped without error
- Empty array (ppfnStart == ppfnEnd) exits immediately
- No parameter validation - assumes valid array bounds

Error Handling:
- No explicit error handling
- Relies on caller to provide valid array bounds
- Function calls are made with no error checking

functions.name: AllocateStackSpace
functions.comment:
Dynamically allocates stack space with page probing to ensure proper memory commitment.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize stack pointer to current position plus 8 bytes (beyond return address and saved ECX)
2. Check if requested allocation size exceeds one page (0x1000 bytes)
3. If multi-page allocation needed, enter probing loop:
   - Subtract one page (0x1000 bytes) from stack pointer
   - Subtract one page from remaining allocation size
   - Touch memory at stack pointer to trigger page commitment
   - Repeat until remaining size is less than one page
4. Subtract final remaining bytes from stack pointer
5. Touch memory at final stack position to commit last page
6. Update ESP register to new stack pointer position
7. Restore original ECX and return address from saved stack frame
8. Return to caller with stack space allocated and committed

Parameters:
dwStackSize (uint) - Number of bytes to allocate on stack

Returns:
void - No return value, modifies stack pointer directly

Special Cases:
- Single page allocations (≤ 0xFFF bytes) skip the probing loop
- Memory touches use TEST instruction to trigger page faults for uncommitted pages
- Stack grows downward, so allocation decreases stack pointer
- Function preserves ECX register across call

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1000 (4096) - Windows page size for stack probing
0xFFF (4095) - Maximum single-page allocation without probing

Error Handling:
- No explicit error handling - relies on Windows page fault mechanism
- Invalid memory access triggers system page fault handler
- Stack overflow protection handled by system guard pages

functions.comment:
Optimized memory move implementation with overlap detection and alignment optimization.

Algorithm:
1. Check for overlapping memory regions (source and destination ranges overlap)
2. If overlapping regions detected, copy backwards from end to start to avoid corruption
3. If no overlap, copy forwards from start to end for better cache performance
4. For both directions, optimize copying using 4-byte aligned transfers when possible
5. Handle misaligned data by copying individual bytes first to reach alignment
6. Perform bulk 4-byte transfers in optimized loop (unroll threshold of 8 iterations)
7. Copy remaining bytes (0-3) using individual byte transfers

Parameters:

pSource - Source memory buffer to copy data from  
dwByteCount - Number of bytes to copy between buffers

Returns:
void * - Returns original destination pointer (pDestination) for function chaining

Special Cases:
Zero byte count - Returns immediately without any memory operations
Misaligned pointers - Falls back to byte-by-byte copying with alignment handling
Large transfers - Uses optimized 4-byte transfers with loop unrolling for performance

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x4 (4) - Alignment boundary and 4-byte transfer size
0x3 (3) - Alignment mask to check 4-byte boundary alignment  
0x7 (7) - Loop unrolling threshold for optimized bulk transfer

Error Handling:
No explicit error checking - assumes valid memory regions and non-null pointers
Overlap detection prevents memory corruption during overlapping copies
Alignment optimization ensures optimal performance on x86 architecture

char *: Pointer to first occurrence of character in string
        NULL if character not found or string is null

Special Cases:
Search character 0x00 finds null terminator location
Optimized for x86 architecture with DWORD-aligned memory access
Uses magic constant 0x7EFEFEFF for simultaneous null detection

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x7EFEFEFF: Magic constant for null byte detection in DWORD
0x81010100: Bit mask to isolate null detection results
0x1010100: Secondary mask for null detection edge cases
0x80000000: Sign bit mask for overflow detection

Performance Notes:
Handles 1-3 unaligned bytes individually for alignment
Processes 4 bytes per iteration in main loop
Returns immediately upon finding target or null terminator

functions.name: CompareStringsIgnoreCase
functions.signature: uint CompareStringsIgnoreCase(void * this, byte * param_1, byte * param_2)
functions.comment:
Performs case-insensitive string comparison with optional locale support

Algorithm:
1. Load saved critical section counter value for potential restoration
2. Check if locale data is available (DAT_6ff39f20 == 0 for simple mode)
3. Simple mode (no locale): Compare characters directly with ASCII case conversion
   - Read characters from both strings until difference found or null terminator
   - Convert to lowercase using ASCII transformation: char + 0xbf + conditional 0x20 + 0x41
   - Return comparison result: -1 if string1 < string2, 0 if equal, 1 if string1 > string2
4. Locale mode: Thread-safe comparison with locale-specific character conversion
   - Increment critical section counter with atomic operation
   - Check critical section depth limit (DAT_6ff3b544)
   - If depth exceeded, restore counter and call error handler FUN_6ff2c3fe(0x13)
   - Compare characters using locale conversion function FUN_6ff2bdda
   - Decrement critical section counter or call cleanup FUN_6ff2c45f(0x13)
5. Return normalized comparison result as unsigned integer

Parameters:
this (pLocaleContext): Locale context object for character conversion operations
lpszString1: First null-terminated string to compare
lpszString2: Second null-terminated string to compare

Returns:
0x00000000: Strings are equal (case-insensitive)
0x00000001: First string is lexically greater than second string
0xFFFFFFFF: First string is lexically less than second string

Special Cases:
- Empty strings (immediate null terminator) return 0x00000000
- Null pointer parameters cause undefined behavior
- Critical section overflow triggers error handler and may modify comparison behavior

Magic Numbers:
0xbf: ASCII case conversion offset (-65 decimal)
0x1a: Check for alphabetic character range (26 decimal) 
0x20: Space character offset for lowercase conversion (32 decimal)
0x41: ASCII 'A' character base (65 decimal)
0x13: Error code passed to critical section handlers
0xff: Initial comparison state marker (255 decimal)

Error Handling:
- Critical section depth limit exceeded: Call FUN_6ff2c3fe(0x13) and restore counter
- Normal exit from critical section: Call FUN_6ff2c45f(0x13) for cleanup
- Locale conversion errors are handled by FUN_6ff2bdda callee

Global Dependencies:
_DAT_6ff3b548: Critical section entry counter (thread synchronization)
DAT_6ff39f20: Locale availability flag (0 = simple mode, non-zero = locale mode)
DAT_6ff3b544: Critical section depth limit threshold

functions.name: AtoiMbcs
functions.comment:
Parse a string to extract an integer value with locale support.

Algorithm:
1. Skip leading whitespace by checking character attribute table for whitespace flag (0x08)
2. Check for optional sign character ('+' = 0x2B or '-' = 0x2D) 
3. Read sign character if found and advance pointer
4. Initialize result accumulator to zero
5. Parse decimal digits by checking character attribute table for digit flag (0x04)
6. For each digit: result = (result * 10) + (digit - 0x30)
7. Continue until non-digit character encountered
8. Apply negative sign to result if minus sign was found
9. Return final integer value

Parameters:
pLocaleContext - LocaleContext pointer for character processing context
pszInput - Pointer to null-terminated string to parse

Returns:
Parsed integer value from string
Positive or negative based on sign character
Zero if no digits found

Special Cases:
Leading whitespace is skipped completely
Plus sign (0x2B) is accepted but does not change result sign
Minus sign (0x2D) negates the final result
Parsing stops at first non-digit character

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x08 - Whitespace character attribute flag
0x04 - Digit character attribute flag  
0x2B - ASCII plus sign (+)
0x2D - ASCII minus sign (-)
0x30 - ASCII zero digit offset for conversion
0x6ff36794 - Global character processing mode flag
0x6ff36588 - Global character attribute table pointer

Error Handling:
No explicit error checking for null pointers
Invalid characters simply terminate parsing
Result defaults to zero if no valid digits found

functions.name: AtoiMbcsWrapper
functions.comment:
Wrapper that forwards a MBCS string to AtoiMbcs for integer conversion.

Algorithm:
1. Push pbStr parameter onto stack
2. Call AtoiMbcs to convert string to integer
3. Return the parsed integer value

Parameters:
- pbStr (byte*): Null-terminated MBCS string to parse

Returns:
- Parsed integer value from AtoiMbcs

Note: Simple thunk function used by ParseTreasureClassItems for parsing
numeric values from treasure class data files.

functions.name: DllMain
functions.comment:
DLL entry point that handles process and thread attach/detach notifications.

Algorithm:
1. Check dwReason parameter to determine DLL notification type
2. DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH (1): Initialize DLL when process loads
   a. Call GetVersion() to get Windows version and store in global
   b. Extract version components: major (low byte), minor (second byte), build (high word)
   c. Store version data in separate globals for compatibility checks
   d. Call initialization routine to verify DLL can load
   e. Get command line with GetCommandLineA() for argument parsing
   f. Initialize core subsystems in sequence
   g. Increment process reference counter
3. DLL_PROCESS_DETACH (0): Cleanup when process unloads
   a. Check if process reference counter is positive
   b. Decrement process reference counter
   c. Check cleanup flag and call cleanup routine if needed
   d. Shutdown subsystems in reverse order
4. DLL_THREAD_DETACH (3): Handle thread cleanup
   a. Call thread-specific cleanup routine with NULL parameter
5. Return appropriate status code

Parameters:
phinstDLL (void *): HINSTANCE handle to DLL instance (Windows opaque handle type)
  IMPLICIT: Parameter passed but not used in this implementation
dwReason (uint): Reason for calling DLL entry point
  - 1 (DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH): Process is loading DLL
  - 0 (DLL_PROCESS_DETACH): Process is unloading DLL  
  - 3 (DLL_THREAD_DETACH): Thread is exiting

Returns:
bool: Success status
  - true (1): DLL initialization/cleanup succeeded
  - false (0): DLL initialization failed, prevent DLL loading

Special Cases:
- DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH: Returns false if version check or initialization fails
- DLL_PROCESS_DETACH: Only performs cleanup if reference counter > 0
- DLL_THREAD_ATTACH (2): Not handled, falls through to return true
- Invalid dwReason values: Fall through to return true

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1 - DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH constant
0x0 - DLL_PROCESS_DETACH constant  
0x3 - DLL_THREAD_DETACH constant
0xff - Byte mask for extracting version components
0x8 - Bit shift for extracting minor version (second byte)
0x10 - Bit shift for extracting build number (high word)
0x100 - Multiplier for combining major and minor version

Error Handling:
- Version API failure: Continues with uninitialized version globals
- Initialization failure: Returns false to prevent DLL loading
- Cleanup errors: No error propagation, always returns true for detach

Type Design Notes:
- HINSTANCE parameter correctly typed as void* (Windows opaque handle convention)
- SSA temporaries (fResult, nTempResult) used for intermediate calculations

functions.name: __amsg_exit
functions.comment:
Exit the application with optional console message display.

Algorithm:
1. Check if console display is enabled by testing DAT_1003c8bc == 1
2. If not enabled, check secondary condition: DAT_1003c8bc == 0 AND DAT_1003c8c0 == 1
3. If either condition true, call FUN_1001f7e7() to display console message
4. Call FUN_1001f820(nExitCode) to perform cleanup operations with provided exit code
5. Call exit function through function pointer PTR___exit_1002e48c with code 0xff
6. Function does not return (terminates process)

Parameters:
nExitCode (int): Exit code to pass to cleanup function FUN_1001f820

Returns:
void - Function does not return (terminates process execution)

Special Cases:
- Always calls exit with hardcoded 0xff regardless of input exit code
- Console message display depends on two global flag variables
- Function pointer call suggests dynamic linking or runtime binding

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1 - Console display enabled flag value
0x0 - Console display disabled flag value  
0xff - Hardcoded exit code passed to exit function (255 decimal)

functions.name: StreamPutChar
functions.comment:
Writes a single character to a stream with buffering and error handling support.

Algorithm:
1. Validate stream flags - check for invalid flag combinations (0x82 clear OR 0x40 set)
2. Handle buffering reset - if 0x01 flag set, reset position and optionally restore buffer base
3. Setup output mode - clear position, set backup pointer, configure output flags (clear 0x10, set 0x02)
4. Validate special streams - check if stream matches standard descriptors and validate with FUN_6ff3037c
5. Perform stream cleanup - call FUN_6ff30338 if validation passes
6. Choose output path - buffered (flags & 0x108 != 0) or unbuffered output
7. Buffered output - calculate available space, write directly to buffer or call write function
8. Handle buffer exhaustion - get stream descriptor from table and check error flags
9. Error handling - call FUN_6ff30070 if error flag 0x20 is set
10. Unbuffered output - call FUN_6ff30148 with character address and size 1
11. Verify write result - compare returned bytes with expected count
12. Set error state - set flag 0x20 on write failure, return character on success

Parameters:
nCharacter: Character to write (only low 8 bits used)
pStream: Pointer to stream descriptor structure

Returns:
Character value (0x00-0xFF) on successful write
0xFFFFFFFF on error or invalid stream state

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x01: Buffer reset flag
0x02: Output mode flag  
0x10: Buffer restore flag
0x20: Error state flag
0x40: Read-only flag
0x82: Combined invalid flags
0x108: Buffering mode flags
0x24: Stream descriptor stride (36 bytes)
0xFF: Character mask for return value
0xFFFFFFFF: Error return value

Structure Layout:
Offset  Size  Field Name    Type      Description
0x00    4     pBase         void*     Base buffer pointer
0x04    4     nPosition     int       Current position offset  
0x08    4     pCurrent      void*     Current buffer pointer
0x0C    4     dwFlags       dword     Primary stream flags
0x10    4     dwFlags2      dword     Stream identifier/handle
0x14    4     reserved      dword     Reserved field
0x18    4     nAvailable    int       Available buffer space
0x1C    4     reserved2     dword     Reserved field  
0x20    4     reserved3     dword     Reserved field

Error Handling:
Invalid flags (0x82 clear OR 0x40 set): Set error flag 0x20 and return 0xFFFFFFFF
Buffer exhaustion with error flag: Call error handler FUN_6ff30070
Write operation failure: Set flag 0x20 and return 0xFFFFFFFF  
Standard stream validation failure: Proceed with cleanup and normal flow

functions.name: FormatStringProcessor
functions.signature: int FormatStringProcessor(int * pOutputHandler, byte * pbFormatString, uint * ppnArgsPtr)
functions.comment:
FormatStringProcessor - processes printf-style format strings with variable arguments

Algorithm:
1. Initialize state variables: dwFlags=0, nStateIndex=0, nCharCount=0
2. Begin character-by-character processing loop of format string
3. For each character, determine processing state using lookup table at 0x6ff333e0
4. Execute state machine transitions based on current state (0-7):
   - State 0: Output literal characters, handle character attributes
   - State 1: Initialize format specifier parsing, reset all flags
   - State 2: Parse format flags: space(0x02), hash(0x80), plus(0x01), minus(0x04), zero(0x08)
   - State 3: Parse field width (decimal digits or asterisk for va_arg)
   - State 4: Encountered decimal point, prepare for precision parsing
   - State 5: Parse precision (decimal digits or asterisk for va_arg)  
   - State 6: Parse length modifiers: I64(0x8000), h(0x20), l(0x10), w(0x800)
   - State 7: Process conversion specifiers and generate output
5. For conversion specifiers: handle integer(d,i,u,o,x,X), float(e,E,f,g,G), character(c,C), string(s,S), pointer(p), written count(n)
6. Apply formatting: field width padding, precision truncation, sign prefixes, case conversion
7. Convert wide characters to multibyte when needed using FUN_6ff30505
8. Output formatted result through pOutputHandler callback
9. Continue until null terminator reached
10. Return total character count

Parameters:
  pOutputHandler (int *) - callback function pointer for character output
  pbFormatString (byte *) - printf-style format string to process
  ppnArgsPtr (uint *) - pointer to variable arguments list array

Returns:
  int - total number of characters processed and output, or negative on error

Special Cases:
  - Field width of -1 indicates unlimited width (0x7fffffff)
  - Precision of -1 disables precision limiting
  - Zero flag (0x08) is ignored when left-align flag (0x04) is set
  - Hash flag (0x80) adds prefixes: "0" for octal, "0x"/"0X" for hex
  - I64 modifier (0x8000) enables 64-bit integer processing

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x6ff333e0 - character classification table for format parsing
  0x6ff33400 - state transition table (8 bytes per character class)  
  0x20/0x78 - valid format character range (space to 'x')
  0x7fffffff - unlimited field width sentinel value
  0x30 - ASCII '0', base for digit conversion
  0x39 - ASCII '9', upper limit for digit checking
  0x2a - ASCII '*', indicates va_arg width/precision
  0x2d - ASCII '-', negative sign character

Error Handling:
  - Invalid format characters fall through to literal output
  - Null string arguments replaced with default "(null)" string
  - Negative field widths converted to left-align with positive width
  - Buffer overflow protection through character count tracking

functions.name: BufferedPutChar
functions.signature: int BufferedPutChar(byte bCharacter, FileBuffer * pBuffer, int * pnCharsWritten)
functions.comment:
Writes a single character to a buffered output stream with automatic flushing.

Algorithm:
1. Decrement the buffer's remaining byte count
2. If buffer has space (count >= 0):
   a. Store character at current buffer position
   b. Increment buffer pointer
   c. Return character value (masked to 8 bits)
3. If buffer is full (count < 0):
   a. Call flush/refill function FUN_6ff2d034
   b. Use its return value as result
4. Check for error condition (-1 return value):
   a. If error: set chars written counter to -1
   b. If success: increment chars written counter

Parameters:
chCharacter (byte) - Character to write to buffer (0-255)
pBuffer (FileBuffer *) - Pointer to buffer structure containing:
  - pbCurrent: Current write position in buffer
  - dwBytesRemaining: Number of bytes left in buffer
pnCharsWritten (int *) - Pointer to character count/status tracker

Returns:
Character value (0-255) on success
-1 (0xFFFFFFFF) on error or buffer flush failure

Special Cases:
If buffer flush operation fails, error state is propagated to caller
Characters are masked to 8 bits (param_1 & 0xff) for return value
Negative buffer count triggers automatic flush/refill operation

Magic Numbers Reference:
0xFFFFFFFF (-1) - Error indicator for failed operations

Structure Layout:
FileBuffer (8 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field Name         Type    Description
0x00    4     pbCurrent          byte*   Current write position
0x04    4     dwBytesRemaining   uint    Bytes remaining in buffer

functions.name: RepeatCharacterToStream
functions.signature: void RepeatCharacterToStream(uint dwCharacter, int nCount, int * pOutputStream, int * pnErrorStatus)
functions.comment:
Writes a specified character to an output stream a given number of times.

Algorithm:
1. Check if repeat count is positive, return immediately if zero or negative
2. Enter loop to repeat character output nCount times
3. Call FUN_6ff2d88d to write dwCharacter to pOutputStream 
4. Check error status after each write operation
5. If *pnErrorStatus equals -1, terminate early with error
6. Decrement count and continue loop if count > 0
7. Exit when all characters written or error encountered

Parameters:
dwCharacter (uint): Character code to repeat (typically ASCII value 0x20 for space, 0x30 for '0')
nCount (int): Number of times to repeat the character 
pOutputStream (int *): Pointer to output stream buffer structure
pnErrorStatus (int *): Pointer to error status flag, set to -1 on write failure

Returns:
void: No return value, error status communicated through pnErrorStatus

Special Cases:
- If nCount <= 0, function returns immediately without writing
- Loop terminates early if write operation sets *pnErrorStatus to -1
- Used for padding in printf formatting (spaces, zeros)

Error Handling:
- Monitors error status after each character write
- Early termination on first write failure (-1 status)
- Calling function must check pnErrorStatus for final status

functions.name: WriteStringToBuffer
functions.signature: void WriteStringToBuffer(char * lpszString, int nLength, FileBuffer * pBuffer, int * pnCharsWritten)
functions.comment:
Writes a string to a buffered output stream character by character with error checking.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that string length is greater than zero
2. Initialize loop variables and counters  
3. For each character in the string:
   a. Decrement remaining character count
   b. Load current character from string pointer
   c. Advance string pointer to next character
   d. Call BufferedPutChar to write character to buffer
   e. Check if write operation failed (error code -1)
   f. If error occurred, exit immediately
   g. If characters remain, continue to next character
4. Return when all characters processed or error encountered

Parameters:
lpszString (char *): Pointer to null-terminated or fixed-length string to write
nLength (int): Number of characters to write from string
pBuffer (FileBuffer *): Pointer to buffered output stream structure
pnCharsWritten (int *): Pointer to counter tracking total characters written

Returns:
void - No return value; error status communicated through pnCharsWritten pointer

Special Cases:
If nLength <= 0, function returns immediately without processing
If BufferedPutChar fails (sets *pnCharsWritten to -1), loop exits early
String pointer is advanced byte-by-byte regardless of character encoding

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1: Byte increment for string pointer advancement (0x6ff2d90d: INC ESI)
-1 (0xFFFFFFFF): Error status code indicating write failure (0x6ff2d91b: CMP dword ptr [EDI],-0x1)

functions.name: ReadAndAdvancePointer
functions.comment:
Reads a 32-bit value from current pointer position and advances the pointer by one element.

Algorithm:
1. Read current value from the pointed-to pointer location
2. Advance the pointed-to pointer by 4 bytes (one uint element)
3. Return the value that was at the original position before advancement

Parameters:
ppuCursor - Pointer to pointer tracking current read position in data stream

Returns:
The 32-bit unsigned integer value that was at the current position before advancement

Special Cases:
This function implements a common "read and advance" pattern used in serialization 
and parsing operations. The caller maintains a cursor pointer that gets automatically
advanced after each read operation.

functions.name: ReadLongLongAndAdvancePointer
functions.comment:
ReadLongLongAndAdvancePointer - reads 8-byte value from variable arguments pointer and advances pointer

Algorithm:
1. Dereference pointer to get current position in arguments array
2. Advance the pointer by 8 bytes (2 * sizeof(uint)) to skip over the 8-byte value
3. Read and return the 8-byte value from the original position before advancement

Parameters:
  ppnArgsPtr (uint **) - pointer to variable arguments array pointer, modified in place

Returns:
  longlong - 8-byte signed integer value read from the arguments array

Special Cases:
  - Used specifically for I64 length modifier in printf format processing
  - Advances pointer by exactly 8 bytes regardless of actual data alignment
  - Reads value from position before advancement (offset -8 from new position)

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x8 - size in bytes of 64-bit value (2 * sizeof(uint))
  -0x8 - negative offset to read value from position before advancement

functions.name: ReadShortAndAdvancePointer
functions.comment:
Reads a 16-bit value from variadic arguments and advances pointer

Algorithm:
1. Advance the arguments pointer by 4 bytes to next argument position
2. Read 16-bit value from previous argument position (offset -4)
3. Combine with high 16 bits of current pointer value
4. Return composite 32-bit value

Parameters:
  ppnArgsPtr (uint **) - pointer to variadic arguments pointer array

Returns:
  uint - composite value with previous 16-bit argument in low bits

Special Cases:
  - Advances pointer before reading value from previous position
  - Combines current high bits with previous low 16 bits using CONCAT22

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x4 - argument stride (4 bytes per 32-bit argument)
  -0x4 - offset to read previous argument position

functions.name: InitializeCriticalSections
functions.comment:
Initialize four critical sections for thread synchronization.

Algorithm:
1. Load InitializeCriticalSection function pointer into ESI register for optimization
2. Initialize first critical section (g_pCriticalSection1) by calling InitializeCriticalSection
3. Initialize second critical section (g_pCriticalSection2) by calling InitializeCriticalSection  
4. Initialize third critical section (g_pCriticalSection3) by calling InitializeCriticalSection
5. Initialize fourth critical section (g_pCriticalSection4) by calling InitializeCriticalSection
6. Restore ESI register and return

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
Function uses register optimization by loading InitializeCriticalSection function pointer 
once into ESI and calling through the register four times instead of direct calls.

Global Variables Referenced:
g_pCriticalSection1 (0x6ff3650c) - Points to first critical section structure
g_pCriticalSection2 (0x6ff364fc) - Points to second critical section structure  
g_pCriticalSection3 (0x6ff364ec) - Points to third critical section structure
g_pCriticalSection4 (0x6ff364cc) - Points to fourth critical section structure

Calling Context:
Called during thread local storage initialization as part of multithreading setup.

functions.name: CleanupCriticalSections
functions.comment:
Cleanup and destroy all thread synchronization critical sections.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize pointer to start of critical section array (0x6ff364c8)
2. Loop through array of critical section pointers until end (0x6ff36588)
3. For each entry, check if pointer is non-null
4. Skip predefined special critical sections (PTR_DAT_6ff3650c, PTR_DAT_6ff364fc, PTR_DAT_6ff364ec, PTR_DAT_6ff364cc)
5. If not special section, delete critical section and call cleanup function FUN_6ff2cac5
6. Advance to next array entry (increment by 4 bytes)
7. After main loop, explicitly cleanup the four special critical sections
8. Return to caller

Parameters:
None - function operates on global critical section array

Returns:
void - no return value, cleanup function

Special Cases:
- Four special critical sections skipped in main loop but cleaned up explicitly at end
- Array spans 0x320 bytes (200 pointer entries) from 0x6ff364c8 to 0x6ff36588
- DeleteCriticalSection function pointer loaded from [0x6ff330d8]

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x6ff364c8 - Start address of critical section pointer array
0x6ff36588 - End address of critical section pointer array  
0x6ff3650c - Special critical section 1 (PTR_DAT_6ff3650c)
0x6ff364fc - Special critical section 2 (PTR_DAT_6ff364fc)
0x6ff364ec - Special critical section 3 (PTR_DAT_6ff364ec)
0x6ff364cc - Special critical section 4 (PTR_DAT_6ff364cc)
0x6ff330d8 - Function pointer to DeleteCriticalSection
0x4 - Pointer size increment for array iteration

Error Handling:
None - assumes all pointers valid, DeleteCriticalSection handles invalid input

functions.name: AcquireCriticalSectionByIndex
functions.comment:
Thread-safe lazy initialization and acquisition of critical section by array index

Algorithm:
1. Calculate pointer to critical section slot in global array g_ppCriticalSections
2. Check if critical section at index is already initialized (non-null)
3. If uninitialized, allocate 0x18 bytes for CRITICAL_SECTION structure
4. If allocation fails, call AmsgExit(0x11) to terminate process
5. Acquire global initialization lock via recursive call AcquireCriticalSectionByIndex(0x11)
6. Double-check critical section is still null (race condition protection)
7. If still null, initialize critical section with InitializeCriticalSection
8. Store initialized critical section pointer in global array
9. If another thread initialized it first, free duplicate allocation with DeallocateMemory
10. Release global initialization lock via FUN_6ff2c45f(0x11)
11. Enter the requested critical section with EnterCriticalSection

Parameters:
nCriticalSectionIndex - Index into global critical section array g_ppCriticalSections
IMPLICIT: Uses global initialization lock at index 0x11 for thread-safe lazy initialization

Returns:
void - Function does not return a value, critical section is held upon return

Special Cases:
Lock index 0x11 (17) is reserved for the global initialization synchronization lock
Process terminates with AmsgExit(0x11) if critical section allocation fails
Double-checked locking pattern prevents race conditions during initialization

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x18 (24 decimal) - Size of Windows CRITICAL_SECTION structure in bytes
0x11 (17 decimal) - Reserved index for global initialization lock

functions.name: ReleaseCriticalSectionByIndex
functions.comment:
Releases a CRT critical section lock by its index.

Classification: Leaf function - wrapper around Win32 LeaveCriticalSection.

Algorithm:
1. Index into g_apCrtLocks array using dwLockIndex
2. Call LeaveCriticalSection on the retrieved CRITICAL_SECTION pointer

Parameters:
  dwLockIndex (uint) - Zero-based index into g_apCrtLocks array

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - No bounds checking on index; caller must ensure valid range
  - Must be paired with prior CRT_EnterCritSectByIndex call

Global Data:
  g_apCrtLocks (0x6fc38644) - Array of LPCRITICAL_SECTION pointers

Called By: 12 functions including CRT_EnterCritSectByIndex, CRT_LeaveCritSectExit

functions.name: InitializeThreadLocalStorage
functions.comment:
Initialize thread-local storage for per-thread context management

Algorithm:
1. Call cleanup routine to prepare for TLS initialization
2. Allocate TLS slot using TlsAlloc(), store in global g_dwTlsSlotIndex  
3. Check if TLS allocation succeeded (index != 0xFFFFFFFF)
4. Allocate ThreadContext structure memory (116 bytes) via custom allocator
5. Verify ThreadContext allocation succeeded (pointer not NULL)
6. Associate ThreadContext with TLS slot using TlsSetValue()
7. Verify TLS value was set successfully
8. Initialize ThreadContext structure with InitializeThreadContext()
9. Get current thread ID and store in context structure
10. Set context flags field to 0xFFFFFFFF (all flags enabled)
11. Store thread ID in first field of context structure
12. Return success status

Parameters:
None

Returns:
bool: true (1) on successful TLS initialization, false (0) on any failure

Special Cases:
If TLS allocation fails (returns 0xFFFFFFFF), function exits immediately with failure
If memory allocation fails, function exits with failure  
If TLS value cannot be set, function exits with failure
Each failure condition branches to common exit_failure label

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x74 (116 decimal): Size of ThreadContext structure allocation
0xFFFFFFFF: Invalid TLS index return value indicating allocation failure
0xFFFFFFFF: Flag mask for enabling all context flags

Error Handling:
TLS allocation failure: return 0
Memory allocation failure: return 0  
TLS value set failure: return 0
All errors result in immediate function exit with false return value

functions.name: TlsCleanupSlot
functions.comment:
Cleans up TLS (Thread Local Storage) resources and calls additional cleanup

Algorithm:
1. Call FUN_6ff2c392() for additional cleanup operations
2. Load current TLS slot index from g_dwTlsSlotIndex global variable
3. Compare slot index against invalid value 0xffffffff 
4. If slot is valid (not 0xffffffff), proceed with TLS cleanup
5. Call TlsFree() with the valid slot index to release TLS slot
6. Set g_dwTlsSlotIndex to 0xffffffff to mark as invalid
7. Return to caller

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
If g_dwTlsSlotIndex is already 0xffffffff (invalid), skip TLS cleanup

Magic Numbers Reference:
0xffffffff (4294967295) - Invalid TLS slot index constant used by Windows API

Error Handling:
No explicit error handling - relies on TlsFree() API behavior

functions.name: InitializeThreadContext
functions.comment:
Initialize thread-specific context structure with SEH error handler table.

Algorithm:
1. Store pointer to global SEH error code table in reserved2 field (offset 0x50)
2. Set reserved1[0xc] field (offset 0x14) to 1 to mark context as initialized
3. Set reserved1[0xd] through reserved1[0xf] fields to 0 for cleanup
4. Return to caller with context structure initialized

Parameters:
pThreadContext - Pointer to ThreadContext structure to initialize

Returns:
void - No return value, initializes context structure in-place

Special Cases:
Magic number 0x1 at offset 0x14 indicates successful initialization state

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name    | Type     | Description
-------|------|---------------|----------|----------------------------------
0x14   | 4    | reserved1[12] | byte     | Initialization flag (1=initialized)
0x15   | 1    | reserved1[13] | byte     | Clear to 0 during initialization
0x16   | 1    | reserved1[14] | byte     | Clear to 0 during initialization  
0x17   | 1    | reserved1[15] | byte     | Clear to 0 during initialization

functions.name: GetOrCreateThreadContext
functions.comment:
Gets or creates the thread-specific context for the current thread.

Algorithm:
1. Preserve current thread error state using GetLastError()
2. Attempt to retrieve existing ThreadContext from TLS using g_dwTlsSlotIndex
3. If no context exists (NULL pointer):
   a. Allocate new ThreadContext structure (116 bytes) via FUN_6ff2cbae
   b. If allocation successful, store context in TLS using TlsSetValue
   c. If TLS storage successful:
      - Initialize the context structure using InitializeThreadContext
      - Get current thread ID and store in context->reserved0 (offset 0x0)
      - Set context flags to 0xFFFFFFFF (offset 0x4)
   d. If allocation or TLS storage fails, call AmsgExit(0x10) to terminate
4. Restore original error state using SetLastError()
5. Return pointer to ThreadContext structure

Parameters:
None

Returns:
ThreadContext* - Pointer to thread-specific context structure
                 Never returns NULL (terminates process on failure)

Special Cases:
- Process termination via AmsgExit(0x10) if memory allocation fails
- Process termination if TLS storage assignment fails
- Error code preservation ensures GetLastError() state is unchanged

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x74 (116 decimal) - Size of ThreadContext structure allocation
0x10 (16 decimal) - Exit code for thread context allocation failure
0xFFFFFFFF - Default flag value set in ThreadContext.dwFlags

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type  | Description
-------|------|------------|-------|------------------------------------------
0x0    | 4    | reserved0  | DWORD | Thread ID storage (misleading field name)
0x4    | 4    | dwFlags    | DWORD | Thread context flags (set to 0xFFFFFFFF)
...    | ...  | ...        | ...   | (Additional fields initialized by InitializeThreadContext)

functions.name: CleanupThreadContext
functions.comment:
Cleanup thread context structure by deallocating all associated memory buffers.

Algorithm:
1. Validate TLS slot index is initialized (not 0xffffffff)
2. Determine thread context pointer from parameter or TLS storage
3. Deallocate memory pointers in reserved1 field at offsets 0x1c, 0x20, 0x28, 0x30, 0x38, 0x3c
4. Check if reserved2 field points to non-default error code array
5. Deallocate custom error code array if not using global default
6. Deallocate the thread context structure itself
7. Clear TLS slot by setting to NULL

Parameters:
pThreadContext: Pointer to ThreadContext structure to cleanup, or NULL to retrieve from TLS

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
If pThreadContext is NULL, retrieves current thread context from TLS storage
If TLS slot is invalid (0xffffffff), function returns immediately
Default error codes array (g_adwSehErrorCodes) at 0x6ff36908 is not deallocated

Magic Numbers Reference:
0xffffffff - Invalid TLS slot index indicating uninitialized TLS
0x1c, 0x20, 0x28, 0x30, 0x38, 0x3c - Offsets to memory buffer pointers in reserved1
0x6ff36908 - Address of global default SEH error codes array (g_adwSehErrorCodes)

functions.name: LocaleMapStringWithConversion
functions.signature: int LocaleMapStringWithConversion(uint dwLcid, uint dwMapFlags, char * lpszSrcStr, int nSrcLen, char * lpszDestStr, int nDestLen, uint dwCodePage, int nFlags)
functions.comment:
Performs locale-aware string mapping with automatic character encoding conversion.

Algorithm:
1. Set up structured exception handling (SEH) frame
2. Initialize Unicode support detection if not already done
   a. Test LCMapStringW with empty string to detect Unicode support
   b. If Unicode fails, test LCMapStringA for ANSI support
   c. Set global flag (1=Unicode, 2=ANSI) based on results
3. Validate source string length using FUN_1001fb97 if positive length
4. Branch based on detected encoding support:
   - If ANSI mode (flag=2): Call LCMapStringA directly and return result
   - If Unicode mode (flag=1): Perform conversion sequence
5. Unicode conversion sequence:
   a. Use default code page if dwCodePage is 0
   b. Calculate required wide character buffer size with MultiByteToWideChar
   c. Allocate stack space for wide character conversion buffer
   d. Convert source string from multibyte to wide character
   e. Get required output buffer size with LCMapStringW
   f. If LCMAP_SORTKEY flag (0x400) is set:
      - Return required size if output buffer is NULL
      - Validate output buffer size and perform mapping directly
   g. If normal mapping:
      - Allocate second stack buffer for wide character output
      - Perform LCMapStringW mapping to wide character buffer
      - Convert result back to multibyte using WideCharToMultiByte
6. Clean up SEH frame and return result

Parameters:
dwLcid (uint): Locale identifier for mapping operation
dwMapFlags (uint): Mapping flags controlling case conversion and sorting
lpszSrcStr (char *): Source string in multibyte encoding
nSrcLen (int): Length of source string (-1 for null-terminated)
lpszDestStr (char *): Output buffer for mapped string
nDestLen (int): Size of output buffer in characters
dwCodePage (uint): Code page for character conversion (0 = default)
nFlags (int): Additional conversion flags for MultiByteToWideChar

Returns:
Number of characters written to output buffer on success
0 on failure (insufficient buffer, conversion error, or unsupported operation)

Special Cases:
If lpszDestStr is NULL, returns required buffer size
LCMAP_SORTKEY flag (0x400) returns sort key instead of mapped string
Automatic fallback from Unicode to ANSI if Unicode APIs unavailable

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x100 - LCMAP_LOWERCASE flag for case conversion test
0x400 - LCMAP_SORTKEY flag for sort key generation
0x220 - WC_NO_BEST_FIT_CHARS | WC_COMPOSITECHECK flags
0x1003ca54 - Global Unicode support flag (1=Unicode, 2=ANSI)
0x1003c8e4 - Default code page storage

Error Handling:
Returns 0 for all error conditions including:
- Unsupported locale or mapping flags
- Insufficient output buffer space
- Character conversion failures
- Stack allocation failures

functions.name: CalculateStringLengthWithLimit
functions.comment:
Calculate the length of a null-terminated string with maximum limit.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize current pointer to start of string and remaining counter to max length
2. If max length is zero, skip to step 5
3. Loop while remaining length > 0:
   a. Decrement remaining length counter
   b. Check if current character is null terminator, if so break loop
   c. Advance current pointer to next character
4. Continue loop until null terminator found or max length reached
5. Check if null terminator was found:
   a. If found: return actual string length (current pointer - original pointer)
   b. If not found: return max length parameter (string exceeds limit)

Parameters:
lpszString (char *): Pointer to null-terminated string buffer to measure
nMaxLength (int): Maximum number of characters to examine before stopping

Returns:
int: Actual string length if null terminator found within limit
     Maximum length parameter if string exceeds specified limit
     Zero if maximum length parameter is zero

Special Cases:
- Returns 0 if nMaxLength is 0 (no characters to examine)
- Returns nMaxLength if no null terminator found within limit
- Handles empty string (immediate null terminator) correctly by returning 0

functions.name: AullDiv
functions.signature: undefined8 AullDiv(uint dwDividendLow, uint dwDividendHigh, uint dwDivisorLow, uint dwDivisorHigh)
functions.comment:
Performs 64-bit unsigned integer division (__aulldiv runtime library function).

Algorithm:
1. Combine 32-bit parameter pairs into 64-bit dividend and divisor values
2. Check if divisor high word is zero (simple 64/32 division case)
3. Simple case: Use 32-bit division operations to compute quotient directly
4. Complex case: Normalize both operands by shifting right until divisor fits in 32 bits
5. Perform approximate division using normalized 32-bit values
6. Multiply trial quotient by original divisor to get product
7. Compare product with original dividend to verify quotient accuracy
8. Decrement quotient if product exceeds dividend (correction step)
9. Return 64-bit quotient as combined high/low 32-bit words

Parameters:
  dwDividendLow   - Low 32 bits of 64-bit dividend
  dwDividendHigh  - High 32 bits of 64-bit dividend  
  dwDivisorLow    - Low 32 bits of 64-bit divisor
  dwDivisorHigh   - High 32 bits of 64-bit divisor

Returns:
  Success: 64-bit quotient (dividend / divisor)
  
Special Cases:
  Division by zero: Undefined behavior (not validated)
  Overflow: Cannot occur with unsigned division
  
Algorithm Details:
  - Uses binary long division when divisor > 32 bits
  - Normalizes operands to avoid overflow during intermediate calculations
  - Trial-and-error approach with correction ensures accuracy
  - Optimized for common case where divisor fits in 32 bits

functions.name: UnsignedLongLongRemainder
functions.signature: undefined8 UnsignedLongLongRemainder(uint dwDividendLow, uint dwDividendHigh, uint dwDivisorLow, uint dwDivisorHigh)
functions.comment:
Calculates 64-bit unsigned remainder (dividend % divisor) using optimized division algorithm.

Algorithm:
1. Check if high 32 bits of divisor are zero for fast path optimization
2. If divisor fits in 32 bits, perform standard division on combined 64-bit dividend
3. Otherwise, normalize operands by right-shifting until divisor fits in 32 bits
4. Perform division on normalized values to get approximate quotient
5. Calculate full product of quotient and original divisor
6. Compare product with original dividend and adjust quotient if needed
7. Subtract final quotient×divisor from dividend to get remainder
8. Return 64-bit remainder as combined high/low 32-bit values

Parameters:
dwDividendLow (uint): Low 32 bits of 64-bit unsigned dividend
dwDividendHigh (uint): High 32 bits of 64-bit unsigned dividend  
dwDivisorLow (uint): Low 32 bits of 64-bit unsigned divisor
dwDivisorHigh (uint): High 32 bits of 64-bit unsigned divisor

Returns:
64-bit unsigned remainder as ulonglong (high 32 bits in EDX, low 32 bits in EAX)
Returns 0 for division by zero (undefined behavior)

Special Cases:
Fast path when dwDivisorHigh == 0: Uses hardware DIV instruction directly
Normalization loop when divisor > 32 bits: Shifts both operands right until divisor fits in 32 bits
Quotient adjustment: If initial quotient estimate is too large, decrements and recalculates

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x20 (32 decimal): Left shift amount for combining high/low 32-bit parts into 64-bit value
0x1f (31 decimal): Right shift amount for propagating carry bit during normalization
0xffffffff: Mask to extract low 32 bits from 64-bit intermediate results
